hints: Focus on what makes a carbon chiral, a carbon attached to four completely different atoms or groups.
Draw out 2-hydroxybutanoic acid as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)COOH}$ and check the four groups on C-2.
Now do the same test for C-3 in compound 2 and for every carbon in $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, then count which molecules have that special carbon.
walkthrough:
**Recall the chiral centre test**

A chiral centre is a carbon with four different groups attached. No symmetry, no two identical H atoms or identical chains.

Rule to apply:
$$\text{chiral C = C bonded to 4 different groups}$$

**Check compound 1: 2-hydroxybutanoic acid**

Draw it out: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)COOH}$. Look at C-2, the carbon bearing the OH.

Its four groups are:
$$\text{-H, -OH, -COOH, -CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
All four are different, so C-2 is chiral. Compound 1 qualifies.

**Check compound 2: 3-hydroxybutanoic acid**

Draw it out: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{COOH}$. Look at C-3, the carbon bearing the OH.

Its four groups are:
$$\text{-H, -OH, -CH}_3\text{, -CH}_2\text{COOH}$$
All four are different, so C-3 is chiral. Compound 2 qualifies.

**Check compound 3: 4-hydroxybutanoic acid**

Draw it out: $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$. Every carbon has at least two identical H atoms.

For example:
$$\text{C-4 = CH}_2\text{OH has two H atoms}$$
No carbon has four different groups, so there is no chiral centre. Only 1 and 2 are correct.

options.A: Incorrect. This suggests all three contain a chiral centre. Compounds 1 and 2 do, but 4-hydroxybutanoic acid has only $\text{CH}_2$ groups, each with two H atoms, so it cannot be chiral.
options.B: Correct. Both 2-hydroxybutanoic acid and 3-hydroxybutanoic acid have a carbon bonded to H, OH and two different carbon chains, giving a chiral centre. 4-hydroxybutanoic acid has no such carbon.
options.C: Incorrect. This would include compound 3 and exclude compound 1. Compound 1 is definitely chiral at C-2, while compound 3 has no carbon with four different groups.
options.D: Incorrect. This would include only compound 1. Compound 2 is also chiral at C-3 because its four groups ($\text{H, OH, CH}_3, \text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$) are all different, so it should not be left out.
